questions.question: When are two systems of equations equivalent?
options: When they have the same solution set.
When their equations are written in the same order.
When they contain the same number of symbols.
When their coefficient matrices have the same entries regardless of right-hand side.
questions.explanation: Two systems are equivalent when they have the same solution set.

questions.skill_detail: conceptual: Definition of equivalent systems.
option_explanations: The order of equations is only a presentation choice: swapping two rows of a system leaves every solution unchanged, so equivalence is governed by the solution set $\{x:Ax=b\}=\{x:Cx=d\}$, not by row order.
The number of symbols is cosmetic: $x=1$ and $2x=2$ use different symbols yet share the solution set $\{1\}$, and equivalence is defined by equality of solution sets, not by symbol count.
Equal coefficient entries regardless of the right-hand side is not the definition.
